what: Series of nightly mean paired differences, with the interval each should produce. What is authored is the series; the arithmetic applied to it is the shipped one.
whatItCannotSay: Nothing about what the lab's own difference series looks like. These say what the interval computes over a series, not what any series is.
whyItIsOwed: Over the captured fixture every band 1 panel is withheld, because one night with no closed horizon cannot produce a series at all. So the block bootstrap and the effective-sample measurement, which are the decision this phase turns on, would be exercised by nothing. The failure that matters here is an interval that is too narrow, and a stage that never computes one cannot be too narrow or too wide.
theSeriesAreGeneratedFromAStatedRecipe: Each series is written out in full so the file is the input rather than a pointer to one, but each was produced by a stated recipe: a mean, a wobble either side of it, an optional AR(1) carry-over, and a fixed seed. The recipe is in the note so a reader can see what shape was intended, and the numbers are what the arithmetic actually ran on. `a-series-that-repeats-itself` needs the carry-over specifically: an independent series has no autocorrelation to measure, so the effective sample comes back equal to the night count and the measurement looks correct while asserting nothing.

scenarios.name: clearly-above-zero
scenarios.why: A series wobbling tightly around a positive mean. The lower bound should clear zero, which is what band 1 reads green on.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.02, wobble +/-0.004, independent nights, seed 1, 40 nights

scenarios.name: straddling-zero
scenarios.why: A series whose mean is barely positive against a wobble ten times its size. The interval should straddle zero and the panel should read that it does not clear it yet. This is the case a too-narrow interval gets wrong, and getting it wrong is how band 1 says the pattern is real before it is.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.001, wobble +/-0.02, independent nights, seed 2, 40 nights

scenarios.name: a-series-that-repeats-itself
scenarios.why: A series where each night carries most of the night before it. The effective sample should fall well below the night count, because nights that repeat each other carry one observation between them however many there are. Without a case of this shape the effective-sample measurement always returns the night count and looks correct.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.01, wobble +/-0.02, AR(1) with rho 0.85 so each night carries most of the one before, seed 3, 40 nights

scenarios.name: too-short-to-say-anything
scenarios.why: Fewer nights than twice the block length, so no interval is produced at all. Withheld rather than printed wide: a panel showing an interval built from a handful of nights invites a reading, and the count beside it is not enough to stop that.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.02, wobble +/-0.005, independent nights, seed 4, 12 nights
